sections.title: Molecular profile of high-grade serous carcinoma
sections.intro: HGSC is a **TP53-mutant, copy-number-driven** carcinoma with low recurrent mutation beyond TP53. About half of tumours are homologous-recombination deficient, and that axis, not histology, stratifies first-line maintenance.
mol: **9% / 8%**, plus somatic BRCA1/2 in an additional **3%**. Germline or somatic BRCA1/2 overall 20%
**11.5%** (56/489), mutually exclusive with BRCA1/2 mutation; survival similar to BRCA wild-type
Among the commonest focal amplifications, **highly amplified in >20%** (with MYC, MECOM). Associated with poor response to primary therapy
HRD-positive incl. BRCAm (myChoice GIS ≥42 or BRCAm)
FRα-high (≥75% of cells PS2+, VENTANA FOLR1-2.1)
**32%** (737/2307 screened; platinum-resistant HGSC, 1–3 prior lines) — MIRASOL supplementary appendix, Fig S1 footnote

**6.7%** by IHC and 10.4% by MSI across all ovarian histotypes (meta-analysis, commonest in endometrioid). In HGSC it is rare: none in an early-stage series, 1/288 in another (a stage IV HGSC, MSH2/MSH6 loss; 1/233 HGSC)
**4.6%** of HGSC (single centre, n=200; mucinous 18.8%; Table 2 — abstract gives 5%/23%); HER2 FISH amplification 11/284 (3.9%; abstract 4%), all HGSC (4.7% of HGSC), in a 288-case series
18% platinum-refractory, 13% platinum-resistant, 2% platinum-sensitive (P=0.049); reversion predicted rucaparib failure (PFS 1.8 vs 9.0 mo, HR 0.12)

notes.title: Practical consequence for testing
notes.html:
1. Test germline and tumour BRCA1/2 and HRD at diagnosis, before the first-line maintenance decision. The PARPi evidence splits sharply into BRCAm / HRD+ non-BRCA / HRD-negative, and the HRD-negative benefit is small or absent.
  2. A BRCA1-methylated tumour is not a BRCA-mutated tumour for prognosis [1]. How methylated tumours behave on PARPi is not settled by the trials tabulated here.
  3. FRα (≥75% PS2+) and PD-L1 CPS matter only at platinum resistance (MIRASOL, KEYNOTE-B96). HER2 IHC is worth doing when T-DXd is on the table, but HER2 3+ is uncommon in HGSC.
  4. MMR testing is low-yield in pure HGSC. Its value is in catching a misclassified endometrioid or mixed tumour.

sections.title: 1. Adjuvant, early stage
sections.intro: FIGO I–II, no gross residual disease after surgery.

rows.name: ICON1 + ACTION combined
rows.regimen: Immediate platinum-based adjuvant chemo vs observation
rows.bio: Serous 34% (300/891 with known histology); grade not split by histology; no effect-size difference by cell type, grade, stage or age

rows.name: ICON1
rows.bio: Serous 32% (144/451 with known histology); grade not split by histology

rows.name: EORTC ACTION
rows.pop: Early-stage EOC; 151 optimally staged, 295 not, 2 unknown
rows.bio: Serous 35% (156/440 with known histology); grade not split by histology
rows.tox: **Benefit confined to non-optimally staged**: in that group, OS HR 1.75 (1.04–2.95) and RFS HR 1.78 (1.15–2.77) against observation; **none if optimally staged**. 10-yr: chemo benefit still restricted to non-optimal staging

rows.name: GOG-157
rows.pop: IA/IB G3, clear cell, IC, completely resected II
rows.bio: **Serous 23%** (clear cell 30%, endometrioid 25%). **Serous, 6 vs 3: recurrence HR 0.33 (0.14–0.77); 5-yr RFS 83% vs 60%**. Non-serous HR 0.94. Serous vs non-serous interaction p=0.04, but 5-histotype homogeneity NS (p=0.285); exploratory

rows.name: GOG-175
rows.regimen: Carbo/paclitaxel ×3 → weekly paclitaxel 40 ×24 wk vs observation
rows.pop: IA/IB G3 or clear cell, IC, II
rows.bio: **Serous 28%** (151/542) (clear cell 31%); serous subgroup HR 0.822 (0.438–1.54), NS

rows.name: ICON7 high-risk early-stage subgroup
rows.pop: FIGO I–IIA grade 3 or clear cell (pre-specified "low-stage high-grade" subgroup; ~9% of ICON7)
rows.bio: Histology within subgroup not reported; no BRCA/HRD
rows.tox: Non-proportional hazards (p=0.002); small numbers, low power

notes.title: Reading Table 1
notes.html:
• The adjuvant chemotherapy benefit in early-stage disease was generated largely in incompletely staged patients. ACTION showed no benefit after optimal staging [14]. The trials predate HGSC being defined as a separate entity. Serous was about a third of patients (ICON1 32%, ACTION 35%, GOG-157 23%, GOG-175 28%), and grade was not reported by histology.
  • The only serous-specific signal is an exploratory GOG-157 subset favouring 6 over 3 cycles (HR 0.33), with a serous vs non-serous interaction of p=0.04 but a non-significant 5-histotype homogeneity test (p=0.285) [17]. It is hypothesis-generating, but it is the reason 6 cycles are usually given for early-stage HGSC.
  • Maintenance after early-stage chemotherapy did not help (GOG-175) [18].
  • Bevacizumab is not supported in high-risk early-stage disease. In ICON7's pre-specified FIGO I–IIA grade 3 / clear cell subgroup (n=142), OS showed no benefit (HR 1.49, 0.53–4.20; deaths 13% vs 8%). The authors conclude these patients "do not seem to benefit", while noting small numbers [34].

rows.name: ICON7

rows.pop: Newly diagnosed FIGO II–IV (III 68%, IV 18%); residual >2 cm 55%
rows.bio: Serous 64% (420/655; low-grade serous excluded as borderline). Post hoc serous/endometrioid PFS HR 0.81 (0.66–1.00)

rows.name: GOG-158

rows.bio: Serous ~72%, G3 ~55%

rows.bio: Serous papillary 44%
rows.tox: Grade ≥2 neuropathy **11% vs 30%**; G4 neutropenic fever 11% vs 2%

rows.name: MITO-7
rows.regimen: Carbo AUC2 + paclitaxel 60 **weekly** ×18 vs q3w AUC6/175 ×6
rows.bio: Serous 70% (564/810); G3 68% (grade missing 19%), not split by histology
rows.tox: QoL better weekly; G≥2 neuropathy 6% vs 17%

rows.name: GOG-262
rows.regimen: Weekly paclitaxel 80 + carbo AUC6 vs q3w paclitaxel 175 + carbo; bevacizumab optional (84% chose it)
rows.pop: Stage II–IV (III 67%, IV 30%); gross residual 63%; NACT 13%

rows.name: ICON8
rows.regimen: q3w carbo/paclitaxel 175 vs q3w carbo + weekly paclitaxel 80 vs weekly carbo AUC2 + weekly paclitaxel 80
rows.pop: FIGO IC–IV, immediate or delayed surgery
rows.bio: **HGSC 69%**; stage IIIC–IV 71%
rows.pfs: 17.7 / 20.8 / 21.0 mo; RMST 24.5 / 24.9 / 25.4 mo, **NS** (non-proportional hazards, so RMST used instead of HR)

rows.name: GOG-252

notes.title: Three traps in Table 2A
notes.html:
1. Dose-dense paclitaxel is a JGOG-3016 result that did not travel. MITO-7, ICON8 (predominantly European, 69% HGSC) and GOG-262 were all negative [25,27,24]. The one concordant signal is GOG-262 without bevacizumab (HR 0.62), a stratified subgroup [24]. Population (Japanese, 55% serous) and the bev interaction are the two leading explanations; neither is proven.
  2. The IP overall survival benefit (GOG-172) was not reproduced in the bevacizumab era. GOG-252 found no PFS or OS difference [29]. iPocc's positive PFS is for IP carboplatin with weekly IV paclitaxel, and its OS was not improved (64.9 vs 67.0 mo; HR 0.95) [30].
  3. Bevacizumab improves PFS, not OS, in unselected newly diagnosed disease. The OS signals are confined to subgroups: GOG-0218 stage IV [32] and ICON7 high-risk (exploratory) [34]. BRCA/HRR status did not predict bevacizumab benefit [32].

sections.title: 2B. First-line maintenance
sections.intro: PARP inhibitors, bevacizumab combinations, immunotherapy. The maintenance choice is a biomarker decision; filter by BRCAm or HRD to see the subgroup HRs that drive it.

rows.name: SOLO1 / GOG-3004
rows.pop: Stage III/IV HGSC or HG endometrioid, **BRCA1/2-mutated**, CR/PR after platinum, no bev

rows.os: 7-yr: median **NR vs 75.2 mo**; **HR 0.55 (0.40–0.76)**, P=.0004 — did not meet P<.0001 (formally NS, prespecified descriptive); **7-yr alive 67.0% vs 46.5%**

rows.pop: Stage III–IV high-grade non-mucinous epithelial OC; ± bev

rows.pop: Stage III/IV with residual or NACT

rows.bio: **HGSC 76%** (762/998); PD-L1+ 49%. BRCA not systematically collected; HRD not assessed

notes.title: ⭐ The first-line maintenance decision is a biomarker decision
notes.html:
BRCA1/2-mutated. Olaparib (SOLO1) gave the largest and most durable effect: 7-year survival 67.0% vs 46.5%, HR 0.55 [36]. It is still formally not significant at the prespecified threshold. Olaparib + bevacizumab (PAOLA-1 tBRCAm HR 0.31) and niraparib (PRIMA BRCAm 0.40) are the alternatives.

HRD-positive, BRCA wild-type. PAOLA-1 is the only trial with an OS signal: HRD+ HR 0.62, 5-year OS 65.5% vs 48.4%, but partly driven by tBRCAm (HR 0.60). In HRD+ non-BRCA the OS HR was 0.71 (0.45–1.13), 5-year 54.7% vs 44.2%, exploratory [37]. PRIMA's HRD+ OS HR was 0.95 [38]. Newer options add to this: DUO-O's non-tBRCAm HRD+ PFS HR 0.49 with the durvalumab + olaparib + bev triplet [43], and the non-BRCA HRD PFS HRs of 0.50–0.58 with PARPi monotherapy (PRIMA, ATHENA-MONO) and 0.43 with olaparib + bev (PAOLA-1). DUO-O HRD+ OS is immature (HR 0.84).

HRD-negative / HR-proficient. PAOLA-1 showed no added olaparib effect (PFS HR 1.00; OS HR 1.19, 0.88–1.63) [2,37]. DUO-O's triplet gave HRD− PFS HR 0.68 but OS HR 0.99 [43]. PRIMA HRP PFS HR 0.68 came with no OS gain (HRP OS 0.93) [38]. ATHENA-MONO HRD− 0.65 and PRIME HRP 0.41 are exploratory [39,42]. For HRP disease, the PFS benefit is real but modest, the OS benefit is unproven, and the toxicity, dose reductions (PRIMA 70.9%) and MDS/AML risk are not modest.

Bevacizumab alone remains an HRD-independent PFS option [31,33].

No PARPi trial has shown an ITT OS benefit. PAOLA-1 ITT 0.92 and PRIMA ITT 1.01, both NS; the PARPi + IO combinations likewise (KEYLYNK-001 ITT 1.04, DUO-O interim 0.95) [44,43]. Placebo arms crossed over to later PARPi at 45.7% and 37.8% [37,38], which confounds OS and is part of why SOLO1's 7-year separation is informative.

Immunotherapy has added nothing on its own in first line (IMagyn050, JAVELIN 100, DUO-O durvalumab arm, KEYLYNK-001 pembrolizumab arm) [46,47,43,44]. Where IO combinations were positive, the PARPi was in the regimen. None has improved OS (DUO-O interim 0.95, KEYLYNK-001 1.04), and FIRST's dostarlimab added only HR 0.85 with no OS difference at interim [45].

sections.title: 3A. Platinum-sensitive recurrence (PFI ≥6 months)
sections.intro: The platinum-free interval decides the regimen class. Three different indications sit here: re-induction chemotherapy ± bevacizumab, PARPi **maintenance** after response, and PARPi **as treatment** instead of chemotherapy.

pre.title: Two boundaries that are easy to cross without noticing
pre.html:
1. Maintenance ≠ treatment. PARPi maintenance after response to platinum (Study 19, SOLO2, NOVA, ARIEL3) is a different indication from PARPi as treatment instead of chemotherapy (SOLO3, ARIEL4, NRG-GY004). The treatment trials gave no OS benefit, and ARIEL4 gave worse OS [69].
  2. "Platinum-resistant" trials exclude refractory disease and cap prior lines (AURELIA ≤2, MIRASOL 1–3, ROSELLA 1–3 with 100% prior bev, KEYNOTE-B96 1–2). Their medians are not expectations for a patient progressing on platinum or after 4+ lines.

notes.title: Reading notes for 3A
notes.html:
• Platinum doublet re-induction is the anchor. ICON4 is the only chemotherapy trial with an OS gain [48]. Carboplatin + PLD is non-inferior with a different toxicity profile [50].
  • Bevacizumab added to re-induction improves PFS, not OS (OCEANS HR 0.95; GOG-0213 P=0.056) [52,53]. It still works after first-line bev (MITO-16B HR 0.51) [54].
  • PARPi maintenance: large PFS effects, no significant final OS in any trial. SOLO2 came closest (HR 0.74, p=0.054) [58]. NOVA non-gBRCA HR 1.06 and ARIEL3 BRCAm 0.83 [60,62]. Crossover to later PARPi confounds every analysis. The benefit is concentrated in BRCAm; HRD− PFS HRs of 0.58 buy little and carry cumulative MDS/AML risk.
  • After a first-line PARPi, rechallenge buys ~1.5–2.5 months (OReO) [65]. That is a different decision from first PARPi exposure.
  • Do not substitute a PARPi for chemotherapy in recurrent disease on current evidence: SOLO3 OS null, ARIEL4 OS worse, GY004 olaparib worse than chemo in non-gBRCAm [67,69,70].

sections.title: 3B. Platinum-resistant recurrence (PFI <6 months)
sections.intro: Primary platinum-refractory disease is excluded from most of these trials. Three regimens now carry an OS benefit over single-agent chemotherapy, each in a defined population; the populations overlap and sequencing is unstudied.

rows.name: ROSELLA
rows.regimen: **Relacorilant 150 mg** (day before, of, after) + nab-paclitaxel 80 D1,8,15 q28d vs nab-paclitaxel 100
rows.pop: PFI <6 mo; 1–3 prior lines; **100% prior bev**; refractory excluded
rows.bio: **HG serous 97%**. BRCAm n=47: PFS HR 1.08 (0.49–2.37); prior PARPi OS HR 0.70 (0.51–0.95) (exploratory)

rows.name: MIRASOL
rows.regimen: **Mirvetuximab soravtansine** 6 mg/kg AIBW q3w vs paclitaxel, PLD or topotecan
rows.bio: BRCAm 14–16%; prior PARPi 55.4%. PFS HR **BRCA+ 0.33 (0.18–0.61)**; BRCA-neg/unknown 0.72 (0.57–0.91) (exploratory)
rows.pfs: **5.62 vs 3.98 mo**, P<0.001; overall HR **not reported** (non-proportional hazards); BICR sensitivity HR 0.72 (0.56–0.92)
rows.tox: ORR 42.3% vs 15.9%; G≥3 AE 41.7% vs 54.1%; blurred vision 40.8%, keratopathy 32.1%

rows.name: KEYNOTE-B96 / ENGOT-ov65
rows.regimen: Weekly paclitaxel ± bev (73%) **+ pembrolizumab** 400 q6w vs + placebo
rows.pop: PFI ≤6 mo; 1–2 prior regimens; refractory excluded
rows.tox: Immune-mediated AE 39%; benefit confined to CPS ≥1

rows.name: AURELIA
rows.regimen: PLD, weekly paclitaxel or topotecan **± bev**
rows.pop: PFI <6 mo; ≤2 prior regimens; refractory, bowel involvement excluded
rows.bio: Serous/adenocarcinoma 84–87%; HGSC share not reported (grade 3 53–58%)

rows.name: NRG-GY003
rows.bio: HGSC 82–86%; PD-L1 not associated with response

rows.name: PLD vs topotecan
rows.bio: Histology not reported
rows.os: Refractory 35.6 vs 41.3 wk, NS; **platinum-sensitive 108 vs 71.1 wk, P=0.008**

rows.name: FORWARD I
rows.pop: Platinum-resistant; FRα positive by the "10×" method
rows.bio: **HGSC 98%**. FRα-high PFS 4.8 vs 3.3 mo, HR 0.69 (0.48–1.00), P=0.049 — **not significant under the testing plan**
rows.tox: Scoring method diluted the effect → PS2+ ≥75% cut-off used in MIRASOL

rows.name: JAVELIN Ovarian 200
rows.bio: **HGSC 69%**; clear cell 13%; refractory 25%. PD-L1+ 57% of 508 evaluable: combination PFS HR 0.65 (0.46–0.92) (exploratory)
rows.pfs: 3.7 vs 3.5 mo; combination HR 0.78 (repeated 93.1% CI 0.59–1.24), **NS**; avelumab alone 1.9 mo, HR 1.68
rows.os: 15.7 vs 13.1 mo; combination HR 0.89, **NS**; avelumab alone 11.8 mo

rows.name: NINJA
rows.bio: Serous 62% (grade not reported); clear cell 21%, OS HR 0.78 (0.46–1.32); PD-L1 TPS ≥1% 39%

rows.name: NRG-GY005
rows.pop: HG serous/endometrioid, platinum-resistant or refractory; no prior PARPi
rows.bio: **HGSC 96.7%** (text; Table 1 serous 91.8%, grade 3 96.7%); gBRCAm 7.8% of tested; primary platinum-refractory 31.6%
rows.os: 12.8 vs 13.6 mo; HR 1.027 (98.3% CI 0.771–1.368), not formally tested

rows.name: Pembrolizumab + bev + metronomic cyclophosphamide
rows.bio: HGSC most common (% in supplement only); BRCAm 35%: ORR 71.4% vs 30.4%
rows.os: Overall median not reported; ≤3 vs >3 prior lines 26.1 vs 12.5 mo, P=.03

rows.name: DESTINY-PanTumor02, ovarian cohort
rows.pop: HER2 IHC 3+/2+; median 3 prior lines (35% ≥5); platinum status not reported
rows.bio: HGSC not reported. **ORR 45.0%; central IHC 3+ (n=11) 63.6%**, IHC 2+ (n=19) 36.8%
rows.tox: ILD 10.5% across cohorts (none fatal in ovarian)

rows.name: Oral etoposide (GOG)
rows.pop: One prior platinum; resistant and sensitive strata
rows.bio: Serous ~65%; grade 3 56%

rows.name: Bevacizumab monotherapy
rows.pop: Platinum-resistant; after topotecan or PLD; ≤3 prior regimens
rows.bio: Serous 82%

rows.name: KEYNOTE-100
rows.pop: Cohort A 1–3 lines PFI 3–12 mo; B 4–6 lines
rows.bio: **HGSC 75%; HGSC ORR 8.5%**; CPS ≥10 ORR 17.1%

notes.title: ⭐ The platinum-resistant decision in 2026
notes.html:
1. Three trials now show an OS benefit over single-agent chemotherapy, each in a defined population:
    • FRα-high: mirvetuximab (MIRASOL), HR 0.67, and fewer grade ≥3 AEs than chemotherapy [4]
    • Prior bevacizumab, 1–3 lines: relacorilant + nab-paclitaxel (ROSELLA), HR 0.65 [74]
    • PD-L1 CPS ≥1: weekly paclitaxel + pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-B96), HR 0.76 [5]
    The populations overlap. No trial compares these regimens with each other, so sequencing is unstudied.
  2. Bevacizumab + chemotherapy improves PFS and palliation (ascites), not OS (AURELIA HR 0.85, 40% crossover) [71]. It is excluded after bowel involvement, and bev monotherapy late in the course carried an 11% perforation rate [84].
  3. Checkpoint monotherapy is inactive (KEYNOTE-100 HGSC ORR 8.5%; JAVELIN 200 avelumab alone HR 1.68; NINJA PFS favours chemo) [79,75,76]. KEYNOTE-B96's benefit required paclitaxel and CPS ≥1: the CPS <1 OS HR was 0.98 [5].
  4. FRα scoring method matters. FORWARD I used a different scoring method and missed its endpoint. MIRASOL's PS2+ ≥75% cut-off is what the OS benefit is attached to [72,4].
  5. HER2 IHC 3+ is uncommon in HGSC, but T-DXd ORR in that small group was 63.6% [80].

sections.title: 4. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (sequencing with cytoreduction)
sections.intro: Covers only the **systemic-therapy sequencing** question (neoadjuvant chemotherapy vs primary cytoreduction) and intraperitoneal chemotherapy at interval surgery. Surgical technique is out of scope.

rows.name: OVHIPEC-1
rows.regimen: 3 NACT → interval surgery **± HIPEC cisplatin 100 mg/m²** → 3 cycles
rows.pop: Stage III, not eligible for primary cytoreduction, ≥SD after 3 cycles
rows.bio: **HGSC ~87–92%**; HGSC PFS HR 0.69 (99% CI 0.48–0.99). BRCA/HRD (post hoc, n=200): BRCAm OS HR 1.73 (0.64–4.72); **BRCAwt-HRD PFS 0.41 (0.20–0.85), OS 0.43 (0.21–0.89)**; HRP OS 0.72; p-interaction 0.016

rows.name: EORTC 55971
rows.regimen: NACT → interval debulking → chemo vs primary debulking → chemo
rows.bio: Serous 62%, undifferentiated 24%; poorly differentiated 41%, grade unknown 41%

rows.name: CHORUS
rows.regimen: 3 cycles → surgery → 3 cycles vs surgery → 6 cycles
rows.bio: **HGSC 73%** + serous grade unspecified 11% (operated patients, local pathology)

rows.name: EORTC 55971 + CHORUS pooled
rows.bio: Histology not reported. **Stage IV: PFS 10.6 vs 9.7 mo, HR 0.77 (0.59–1.00); OS 24.3 vs 21.2 mo, HR 0.76 (0.58–1.00)** favouring NACT

rows.name: JCOG0602
rows.regimen: 4 TC → interval debulking → 4 TC vs primary debulking → 8 TC
rows.bio: Serous 78% (grade not reported); clear cell/mucinous 4.6% NACT vs 9.5% PDS, disadvantaged with NACT
rows.os: 44.3 vs 49.0 mo; HR 1.052 (90.8% CI 0.835–1.326); **non-inferiority not confirmed**

rows.name: SCORPION
rows.regimen: NACT → interval debulking vs primary debulking
rows.pop: IIIC–IV, high tumour load (laparoscopic PI 8–12); single centre
rows.tox: Early major complications (patients) **9.5% vs 46.4%**, P<0.0001; postoperative deaths 0 vs 8.3%

rows.name: KOV-HIPEC-01
rows.pop: Stage III–IV, residual <1 cm after primary or interval surgery
rows.bio: Serous 86–92% by arm; post-NACT HGSC PFS HR 0.49 (0.28–0.88) (subgroup)
rows.pfs: ITT 19.8 vs 18.8 mo (P=.43), **NS**; interval-surgery subgroup 17.4 vs 15.4 mo, HR 0.60 (0.37–0.99)
rows.os: ITT 69.5 vs 61.3 mo (P=.52), NS; interval subgroup 61.8 vs 48.2 mo, HR 0.53 (0.29–0.96)
rows.tox: Overall negative; interval benefit is subgroup-only

rows.name: TRUST / ENGOT-ov33
rows.regimen: Primary vs interval cytoreduction at certified centres
rows.tox: **No peer-reviewed results indexed (2026-09-14)**; design paper only

notes.title: Reading Table 4
notes.html:
• NACT is non-inferior for OS in two RCTs [85,86] with less perioperative morbidity. JCOG0602 did not confirm non-inferiority [88]. The pooled analysis favours NACT in stage IV [91].
  • HIPEC with cisplatin at interval cytoreduction after NACT is the one setting with a randomized OS benefit (OVHIPEC-1, HR 0.70 at ~10-year follow-up) [94]. KOV-HIPEC-01 was negative overall, with a supporting interval-surgery subgroup [95].
  • Neoadjuvant patients are eligible for first-line PARPi maintenance. PRIMA enrolled any-NACT patients as "high risk" [3]. The maintenance decision in Table 2B does not change with sequencing.
